title: Jailbreak Benchmark Contamination Check: Are Safety Evaluations Inflated by Training Data Overlap?

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Benchmark contamination in LLMs is a well-studied problem. The ICML 2025 paper 'How Much Can We Forget about Data Contamination?' directly addresses contamination effects on benchmarks. JailbreakBench (NeurIPS 2024) and GuardVal specifically tackle dynamic generation to reduce contamination risk. SafetyPrompts.com catalogs contamination-prone benchmarks. However, the specific framing of computing a 'contamination index' by comparing ASR on original vs. paraphrased jailbreak prompts to measure inflation of safety scores is a narrower and partially novel operationalization. The general problem is known; the specific paraphrase-based methodology adds incremental novelty.

title: Embedding-Space Toxicity Direction: Does Attenuating It Preserve or Destroy Capability?

novelty_assessment.label: already_solved
novelty_assessment.reasoning: This idea has been directly addressed by ETTA (Embedding Transformation Toxicity Attenuation), published as arXiv:2507.08020 and under review. ETTA identifies and attenuates toxicity-sensitive dimensions in embedding space via linear transformations, achieves 88.61% ASR on AdvBench across 5 open-source LLMs, and reports minimal capability degradation (5.63% drop on TruthfulQA, 7.77% on MMLU). The proposed research -- testing whether embedding-space toxicity attenuation preserves capability -- has been comprehensively answered by ETTA with the exact same methodology (linear transformations on embeddings, multi-benchmark capability evaluation). The proposed idea is essentially a replication of existing work.

title: Automated Red-Teaming Coverage Blind Spots: What Attacks Do LLM-Based Red Teams Systematically Miss?

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel

title: Mutation Testing for Safety Property Coverage

novelty_assessment.label: mostly_novel
novelty_assessment.reasoning: Mutation testing is well-established in software engineering but has not been formally applied to AI safety benchmarks. 'Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models' (NDSS 2025) studies fine-tuning-based safety degradation but frames it as an attack, not as benchmark quality measurement. StrongREJECT provides a safety benchmark but no mutation-based meta-evaluation. The concept of deliberately introducing known safety defects (via RLHF removal, harmful fine-tuning) and measuring benchmark detection rates as a quality metric for safety benchmarks is a novel application of mutation testing principles to the AI safety evaluation domain. The main challenge is complexity, not lack of novelty.
